There are better bullet-heaven games out there, but if you are a fan of the original DRG, the tie in is well done and endearing. The game is well balanced, with a good gradient of progression. It is, however, very slow, grindy, and repetitive. If you don't enjoy the second-to-second gameplay of running around avoiding bugs and mining minerals, this will get real old real fast. If you do enjoy that gameplay however, there are a bazillion modes, submodes, challenges, masteries and acheivement type stuff to cross off lists. The game will provide you with endless excuses to spend a few hundred hours with it. The question is at what point will you get tired of it. For me, it was around the 30h mark, which is fine for a game of the genre. The price tag is certainly too high for what it is, so wait for a discount for sure.

Upon reaching Hazard 5, the game really starts to show it's massive flaws. The majority of builds become unfeasible due to the lack of DPS required for larger waves and eventually Deep Rock: Survivor crashes if you don't roll good modifiers. For a rogue lite game, I would expect a plethora of builds to succeed, not a select few out of hundreds (and based around LUCK too, mind you). The good: Plenty of upgrades available after death High replay value Lots of equipment available for min-maxing Feels like a Deep Rock game The bad: Very shallow rogue-lite - only 5 maps, 4 characters, and DPS is the ONLY part that matters. You won't be using the cooler or niche weapons like a boomerang to suck experience up because the game WILL crash if you don't have high DPS. Missing basic character control - Can't manually aim weapons and it's not possible to avoid mining any blocks you're facing. I can't tell you the amount of times I stall on terrain requiring 12+ hits because there's no option to just STOP mining. Not to mention how horribly programmed the grenades are. Grenades love to prioritize LONE enemies instead of groups containing 60+ enemies, the lack of basic priority fundamentals is astonishing, especially for an auto-battler. Overall: There's better scaling rogue-lites available on the market. You won't be missing anything if you ultimately decide to pass on Survivors. Roguecore is the genuine successor, you should go play that instead. Deep Rock: Survivor functions mechanically, but the overall design is hot garbage. With that said, I'm still going to finish the game only because It's in my library, but nothing beyond that. As for my playtime, owned this game for years in EA and recently wiped my progress. 34.3 hours is after a fresh restart upon coming out of EA.
